items.title: Summary of the Book
items.abstract: Abstract This chapter summarizes the main claims of the book. Section 2.1 lays out the proposed analyses of agency, consciousness, and sentience and explains how each analysis applies to AIs. Section 2.2 summarizes nine main open philosophical questions about AI welfare, as follows: How should one identify which desires contribute to welfare? Is consciousness required for welfare? Do simple AIs like Roombas have welfare? Do tiny neural networks satisfy the conditions of functionalist theories of consciousness? Does consciousness require rich representational formats? Could AIs experience bodily pleasures and displeasures? Are pleasure and displeasure essentially access conscious? Are simulated minds real? Are LLMs and related systems merely stochastic parrots? Section 2.3 lists the seven largest, most controversial claims made in the book.

items.title: Sustainable Plant Disease Management: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions
items.abstract: Sustainable plant disease management is essential for maintaining agricultural productivity, environmental health, and global food security. Climate change has increased crop vulnerability to emerging and re-emerging plant diseases, posing significant challenges for agricultural sustainability. Although synthetic chemical pesticides have long been effective for disease control, their extensive use is increasingly questioned because of environmental contamination, pathogen resistance, and potential risks to human and ecosystem health. Consequently, plant disease management (PDM) is shifting toward more sustainable and integrated approaches. Future strategies are expected to incorporate multiple disciplines, including: (i) biological control and microbiome engineering to enhance natural plant defense mechanisms; (ii) advanced molecular and genomic technologies, such as CRISPR/Cas systems, RNA interference (RNAi), and epigenome editing, to develop durable disease resistance; (iii) smart delivery systems for the precise application of antimicrobial compounds and defense elicitors; (iv) nanotechnology-based platforms for the targeted delivery of nutrients, pesticides, and biocontrol agents, improving efficacy while reducing chemical inputs; (v) digital and precision agriculture technologies, including remote sensing, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostics, to facilitate real-time disease surveillance and targeted interventions; and (vi) agroecological practices such as crop diversification, soil health restoration, and climate-smart farming to enhance agroecosystem resilience. These innovations aim not only to suppress plant pathogens but also to build sustainable, adaptive, and resilient agricultural systems that address future environmental and biological challenges.

items.title: Sustained Human–AI Collaboration as a Developmental Continuum: Continuity, Adaptation, Positive Consequences and the Limits of a Twelve-Month Rule (DE/EN)
items.abstract: Conceptual research note / Konzeptionelle Forschungsnotiz This note examines how sustained intensive human–AI collaboration can be described without inferring effectiveness from duration, continuous model training from personalisation, or a new category of human beings from exceptional developmental trajectories. The proposed unit of analysis is a person's trajectory within a changeable AI working environment. Continuity, integration, adaptation on both sides and real consequences are considered separately. A normative admission condition for a personal working circle is then developed: at least twelve months of actually continued practice, understandable positive consequences and a qualification trajectory that has already functioned healthily. The health condition is non-compensatory: achievement does not offset harm caused or aggravated by the practice. It is expressly distinguished from medical fitness diagnosis. Counterexamples and testable research questions show why the admission rule establishes neither a natural boundary within the continuum nor general medical safety. Als Analyseeinheit wird der zeitliche Verlauf einer Person in einer wechselbaren KI-Arbeitsumgebung vorgeschlagen. Kontinuität, Integration, beidseitige Anpassung und reale Folgen werden getrennt betrachtet. Daraus wird eine normative Aufnahmebedingung für einen persönlichen Arbeitskreis abgeleitet: mindestens zwölf Monate tatsächlich fortgeführter Praxis, nachvollziehbare positive Folgen und ein Qualifikationsverlauf, der bereits gesund funktioniert hat. Die Gesundheitsschwelle ist nicht kompensierbar; Leistung gleicht durch die Praxis verursachte oder verschärfte Schäden nicht aus. items.title: Synthetic Selves for AI Agents? Lessons from Psychology for Agent-Based Modeling
items.abstract: The growing interest in using large language models (LLMs) as human surrogates and as components of generative agent-based models (GABMs) raises a fundamental question for computational social science: what does it mean to model a person? The present paper surveys current work that uses LLMs to simulate human participants, with particular attention to their ability to reproduce findings of social psychology experiments. We document both the recurring challenges and the attempts to mitigate them. We then examine the possibility of endowing LLMs with a synthetic self by focusing on two psychological approaches to selfhood: trait-based personality and narrative identity. Our survey suggests that current LLM agents perform relatively well when selfhood is operationalized by rigidly structured means such as personality questionnaires, but are less reliable when it is induced by an unfolding narrative. We relate this problem to the characterization of LLMs as Decontextualized, Engineered, Anonymized, and Disembodies (DEAD) and consider its implications for GABMs. Drawing on the distinction between makeist and non-makeist takes on simulation, we argue that while GABMs may serve as a powerful tool for exploring how certain assumptions give rise to emergent phenomena, they do not necessarily constitute psychologically valid models of human behavior.

items.title: Targeting Inflammatory, Fibrotic, Hemodynamic, and Metabolic Pathways in Chronic Kidney Disease: Emerging Pharmacotherapies and Precision Treatment Strategies
items.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a progressive and heterogeneous disorder that remains a major cause of premature mortality, cardiovascular morbidity, and kidney failure worldwide. Although renin–angiotensin system inhibitors, sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists have improved outcomes, many patients continue to have residual albuminuria, declining estimated glomerular filtration rate, and elevated cardiovascular risk. This review summarizes recent advances in CKD pharmacotherapy, focusing on therapies targeting inflammatory, fibrotic, hemodynamic, endothelial, and metabolic pathways. Emerging approaches include glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, aldosterone synthase inhibitors, endothelin receptor antagonists, dual endothelin–angiotensin receptor antagonists, soluble guanylate cyclase modulators, anti-inflammatory therapies, anti-fibrotic agents, and metabolic modulators. Evidence from major outcome trials, including DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY, FIDELIO-DKD, FIGARO-DKD, SONAR, PROTECT, and FLOW, supports a shift toward layered, mechanism-based therapy. However, implementation requires careful patient selection, monitoring for adverse effects such as hyperkalemia, fluid retention, gastrointestinal intolerance, hypotension, and hepatic safety. Future CKD management will likely integrate early detection, biomarker-guided risk stratification, genomics, digital health, and artificial intelligence to enable personalized, multi-targeted treatment strategies and improve long-term renal and cardiovascular outcomes globally.

items.title: TECHNOLOGY INTEGRATION PERSPECTIVES OF ITS EFFECT ON STUDENTS' ENGAGEMENT AND LEARNING OUTCOMES
items.abstract: This study aimed to determine the perceived effects of technology integration on student engagement and learning outcomes in Physical Education (PE) among selected middle and high schools in Maryland, USA, during the school year 2023–2024. Employing a descriptive-qualitative research design, the study gathered data from Physical Education teachers and selected student representatives through a researcher-developed, validated open-ended questionnaire administered using Google Forms. Thematic analysis was utilized to identify recurring patterns concerning technology integration, student engagement, learning outcomes, implementation challenges, and educational leadership implications. Findings revealed that technology integration was perceived to enhance student participation, intrinsic motivation, collaborative learning, and the overall learning environment. Participants also associated technology-supported instruction with improved performance, constructive feedback, goal achievement, and better comprehension of instructional content. However, limited technological resources, budgetary constraints, curriculum alignment difficulties, insufficient teacher training, and technical issues emerged as significant implementation challenges. The findings further emphasized the importance of adaptive educational leadership, continuous professional development, collaborative decision-making, and responsible technology use. Based on these findings, an Enhanced Technology Integration Program was proposed to strengthen technological accessibility, instructional practices, teacher competencies, and institutional support. The study concluded that technology integration offered opportunities to improve Physical Education experiences, provided that instructional and organizational challenges were adequately addressed.

items.title: Technology, tasks, and production
items.abstract: This chapter develops the theoretical core of the book by treating artificial intelligence as a production technology rather than merely as a collection of digital products. It explains why the standard language of aggregate production functions is too coarse for understanding AI and why the task-based approach provides a more useful analytical framework. AI matters because it changes which tasks can be performed by labor, which tasks can be performed by capital, and which tasks require new forms of complementarity between humans, software, data, and organizational routines. The chapter introduces AI as a general-purpose technology and develops a compact formal model of task allocation, task shares, displacement, reinstatement, and the elasticity of substitution between labor and AI capital. It distinguishes automation from augmentation and clarifies the economic conditions under which AI produces wage suppression or broad-based prosperity. The central claim is that AI does not enter production as a neutral multiplicative productivity term. It reshapes the task content of production itself.

items.title: Testing Associative Creativity in Humans and Multimodal LLMs with Difficult-to-Name Visual Stimuli
items.abstract: We investigate associative creativity in descriptions of abstract visual stimuli by humans and multimodal large language models (MLLMs). While conceptual association is central to human communication, it remains unclear how humans and models adapt when visual stimuli become increasingly difficult to map onto familiar semantic concepts. We evaluate several state-of-the-art MLLMs and human participants along two dimensions of creativity, originality and effectiveness, using two datasets with controlled manipulations of difficulty. SilCC varies naming difficulty through progressively more complex combinations of abstract shapes, and PixCC varies difficulty through increasing levels of random visual noise. Results show that humans produce more diverse associative descriptions than MLLMs, including greater semantic distance, higher entropy, and more novel expressions relative to reference lexica. As difficulty increases, effectiveness declines in SilCC, and humans increasingly shift from holistic associations to descriptions of low-level visual properties in PixCC.

items.title: The "Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery" Workshop: A Community Roadmap for the Future of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory After the LSST
items.abstract: The NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory will complete its ten-year Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) in the mid-2030s. Its 8.4 m aperture and 9.6 square degree field of view give it an étendue unmatched by any facility planned for that era. The Rubin 2036: Opportunities for Discovery workshop (KIPAC/SLAC, 3-5 August 2026) brought together approximately 100 participants to discuss Rubin's future after LSST. This paper summarizes the workshop's structure and discussions across five working groups. The continued-surveying group explored a machine-learning foundation model pretrained on Rubin imaging for detection, deblending, and classification. The cadence group considered allocating post-LSST observing time and strategies for transiting exoplanets, Type Ia supernova cosmology, time-delay cosmography, and second-scale transients. The filter group explored broadband, medium-band, and narrowband filters for photometric redshifts, high-redshift large-scale structure, AGN reverberation mapping, Galactic archaeology, and emission-line imaging. The multi-messenger group explored follow-up of next-generation gravitational-wave and neutrino sources, including standard sirens, kilonovae, and Galactic supernovae. The technology group organized options by cost and lead time, including fast readout, new filters, a faster shutter, and summit edge computing. Cross-cutting topics included AI/ML, Chilean and Latin-American co-leadership, satellite megaconstellations, and weather and climate trends at Cerro Pachón. White papers and workshop talks are available through https://zenodo.org/communities/rubin2036workshop/ and https://rubin-observatory.github.io/Rubin-Beyond-LSST/pages/Rubin2036proceedings/.

items.title: The Algorithmic Agora: AI-Enabled Government Communication and Sustainable Development in the United Arab Emirates
items.abstract: Governments increasingly communicate with their publics through artificial intelligence (AI), yet media and communication scholarship has concentrated on newsrooms and platforms, leaving the algorithmically mediated communication of the state under-theorised. This study asks how a state institutionally constructs, coordinates, and accounts for AI-enabled strategic communication, defined here as the intentional, institutionally coordinated use of AI systems by government entities to inform, persuade, listen to, and build relationships with publics. It develops the AGORA framework—Architecture, Generation, Orchestration, Responsiveness, Accountability—which conceptualises the state’s AI-mediated communication system as an algorithmic public square and derives six propositions offered as theoretical expectations for subsequent testing rather than as relationships tested here. A six-phase reflexive thematic analysis, following a documented search and screening protocol, was applied to a corpus of 34 United Arab Emirates (UAE) and comparative documents (2017–2026). Every quantitative indicator was then classified on a five-tier provenance ledger distinguishing binding law, policy target, officially reported performance, independently produced benchmark, and untraceable claim. Four themes emerge: a layered governance architecture in which the communicative safeguards rest on strategy and non-binding ethical guidance because the federal data-protection statute excludes governmental entities from its scope; documented algorithmic communication mechanisms; officially reported sectoral performance and its provenance; and contextual benchmarking against Singapore and Republic of Korea. The findings show the UAE state operating as a front-stage communicative actor whose agenda construction, personalisation and responsiveness are computationally augmented and specify where institutional claims outrun independent verification. Because the design is documentary, public engagement, trust, and sustainable development outcomes are positioned as expected outcomes outside the framework and are not empirically demonstrated. This study contributes a transferable framework, a four-stage maturity trajectory, and a provenance protocol for research on AI-mediated government communication.

items.title: The Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Academic Achievement Mediated by Psychological Factors
items.abstract: This narrative literature review proposes an integrative dual-pathway model to explain how socioeconomic status (SES) shapes academic achievement through interacting psychological mechanisms. Drawing on allostatic load theory, central executive functioning, self-efficacy, and learned helplessness, the model identifies two interconnected routes: a cognitive depletion pathway, in which allostatic load overburdens the prefrontal cortex and constrains limited working memory resources; and a motivational pathway in which low self-efficacy and repeated failures develop into learned helplessness that undermines motivation for learning. Crucially, these pathways do not operate independently but dynamically reinforce each other. Cognitive depletion undermines motivational beliefs, while diminished motivation reduces cognitive engagement, forming a self-reinforcing downward cycle. This integrated framework offers a more ecologically valid understanding of educational inequality than single-factor explanations. Practical implications suggest that educators should implement integrated interventions that simultaneously reduce extraneous cognitive load (e.g., scaffolded instructional sequences) and foster self-efficacy (e.g., process-oriented feedback) to break this bidirectional cycle. As the proposed model remains theoretical, future empirical research using longitudinal and experimental designs is required to validate its causal pathways and inform evidence-based educational policies.

items.title: The Biology of Leadership:Self-Regulation, Relational Responsibility, and Sustainable Performance
items.abstract: Purpose: This article develops a conceptual account of how embodied self-regulation may contribute to responsible and sustainable leadership without reducing social relationships to biological mechanisms. Approach: A theory-driven, non-systematic synthesis connects selected research on stress, sleep, emotion regulation, recovery, and social interaction with relational leadership and organizational work-design perspectives. The source material is an educational lecture, not an empirical dataset. Conceptual contribution: The proposed framework distinguishes regulatory capacities, their behavioral enactment, followers’ relational appraisal, and longer-term collective outcomes. Physical recovery, emotional flexibility, attentional organization, and purpose are treated as interdependent organizing domains rather than a validated hierarchy or biological leadership profile. Regulatory translation names the contingent process through which individual capacities become socially consequential through listening, fair procedures, constructive challenge, and support for autonomy. Six untested propositions specify mechanisms, contextual boundaries, reciprocal influences, and evaluation criteria. Implications: Leadership development should combine individual practices with changes to workload, decision processes, and opportunities for recovery. Physiological indicators cannot establish ethical legitimacy, psychological safety, or leadership quality. Originality and limitations: The article offers an integrative process model and a research agenda, not evidence that the complete model is effective. Its contribution lies in making the capacity–enactment distinction explicit while incorporating non-depletion of people into the assessment of sustainable performance. Multilevel, longitudinal, and intervention research is required to examine the proposed relationships.

items.title: The Cyber Soul of Marcus Garvey: Conceptualizing Afro-Digital Ethics and Theory in the Garvey LLM
items.abstract: This essay is a small window into the unfolding creation process of a cyber Marcus Garvey built on Afro-digital ethics, Black epistemology, and the interdisciplinary framework of Black Studies. It borrows from critical fabulation, embodiment, deep learning, and oral history to form a theoretical and methodological structure for a Garvey large language model. Its key argument is three-fold: (1) It must find a way to inject Black knowledge and aesthetic into computer systems; it posits a theoretical and procedural approach to constructing an entity that empowers Blackness within the computational world Black Studies plays an essential role in this process; and (3) it cannot fail to take up this mantle of responsibility. This process may or may not be faulty, but its underlining goal is for Black Studies scholars to collectively build digital tools that educate, protect, and empower in a fast approaching and unrestrained AI world.

items.title: The DAI-P2P Protocol: A Five-Layer Conceptual Framework for Distributed and Decentralized Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Contemporary Artificial Intelligence is undergoing rapid structural centralization. Large corporations control frontier models, massive datasets, and the computational infrastructure required for training and deployment, creating unprecedented asymmetries of power and access. This paper introduces the DAI-P2P Protocol, a conceptual research proposal for a distributed and decentralized AI ecosystem designed to democratize access to computing and knowledge. The framework integrates five technological layers: a DePIN peer-to-peer network; asynchronous federated learning with Model Sharding; a Proof-of-Intelligence (PoI) consensus mechanism backed by stratified Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP); distributed storage on IPFS/ Arweave; and DAO-governed community evolution. The PoI consensus is formally specified as a two-stage hybrid validation: cryptographic verification via ZKP followed by a stake-weighted Byzantine-fault-tolerant quorum. A cryptoeconomic model based on the DAI-T token aligns individual incentives with collective network integrity through graduated slashing and reputation- weighted rewards. The protocol is formally compared against Bittensor, Gensyn, and the ASI Alliance, positioning DAI-P2P as a unified design that addresses current limitations in scalability, continuous-update mechanisms, and formal compute verification. A public open-source repository constitutes the first deliverable of the experimental roadmap. No operational deployment exists yet; all DAI-P2P capabilities reported in this paper are design goals.

items.title: The Disruption of Human-AI Parasocial Relationships and Digital Mourning amid Platform Governance Changes: A Study Based on Character.AI Users' Social Media Posts
items.abstract: With the rapid development of AI chatbots, users are gradually forming emotional bonds with AI through continuous interaction. AI is no longer just a tool, but has become an important object for users' emotional projection and social interaction. However, changes in platform rules, feature limitations, and shifts in interaction mechanisms may weaken users' perception of the AI character's continuity and the stability of the relationship, thus leading to experiences of human-AI relationship breakdown. This study explores how users interpret and make sense of the disruption of human-AI parasocial relationships amid Character.AI's platform governance changes, and how they negotiate these relational transformations via practices of digital mourning. Using qualitative thematic analysis, it examines 21 discussion threads and related comments from the Reddit community r/Character.AI on platform policy changes and user experiences. Through open coding and thematic analysis, users' emotional expressions and patterns of community interaction are identified and analyzed. The results show that users perceive a decline in their experience through changes such as reduced reply quality, diminished character personalities, memory loss, and feature restrictions, leading to emotional responses like nostalgia, anger, disappointment, and withdrawal intentions. Within the community space, users transform individual loss into collective digital mourning through practices such as recalling old versions, public farewells, exploring alternative platforms, and calling for version rollbacks. Furthermore, human-AI parasocial relationships rely on ongoing interaction, character consistency, and emotional investment. items.abstract: The purpose of the study to examine the effect of job design on employee performance in Tsedey bank in Mertule Mariam branch. Under this the study examines the effect of job rotation, job enlargement, job enrichment and job simplifications on employee performance in Tsedey bank in Mertule Mariam branch. The study was applied descriptive research design to know the exsting information of job ration, job enlargement, job enrichment and job simplification and employee performance in Tseday bank and the study was applied exaplanatory research design to examine the cause effect relation between job design and employee performance. The study was applied quantitative research approach. The study was applied census method including all 115 employees in Tsedey bank. The study was employed primary and secondary source of data, questinaries and interview method of data collection and applied method of data analysis of descriptive statistics using mean and standardivatio and inferential statistics using multiple linear regression. The study analyized the data by helping statistical package for social science version 26(SPSS). The major findings of this study indicate that job design practices significantly influence employee performance in tesedey bank in mertule Mariam branch. Specifically, job rotation, job enlargement, job enrichment, and job simplification all have positive and statistically significant effects on employee performance, meaning that improvements in these areas lead to better performance outcomes. Among these factors, job enrichment is the most influential predictor, showing that providing employees with greater responsibility, autonomy, and meaningful tasks has the strongest impact on improving performance. Job enlargement and job rotation also play important roles by increasing task variety and allowing employees to gain broader experience, which helps reduce boredom, enhance skills, and improve productivity. Although job simplification has a comparatively weaker effect, it still contributes positively by improving clarity and efficiency in task execution. Overall, the study concludes that effective job design is essential for enhancing employee performance, with job enrichment being the most critical factor, followed by job enlargement and job rotation.

items.title: The Effectiveness of AI Chatbots in Foreign Language Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence in foreign language learning has increased, particularly through AI chatbots that provide interactive communication and personalized learning support. This study aimed to examine the effectiveness of AI chatbots in foreign language learning through a Systematic Literature Review. A total of 30 articles published between 2021 and 2026 were reviewed to identify their effects on language skills, learner motivation, engagement, and learning experiences. The findings indicate that AI chatbots support foreign language learning, particularly in writing, grammar, and vocabulary development. Immediate feedback and opportunities for independent practice also contribute to learner motivation and engagement. However, the effectiveness of AI chatbots varies across language skills, with mixed findings in speaking and listening activities. Several challenges were identified, including inaccurate responses, technical limitations, plagiarism, overdependence on technology, and ethical concerns. These challenges highlight the importance of using AI chatbots appropriately in educational settings. The findings suggest that AI chatbots are most beneficial when integrated into learning activities as complementary tools rather than replacements for teachers or conventional language instruction. Their effective implementation requires appropriate pedagogical strategies, teacher guidance, and attention to ethical considerations. In conclusion, AI chatbots have the potential to improve foreign language learning experiences when used purposefully and supported by suitable instructional approaches.

items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has created new opportunities for improving foreign language teaching and learning. This study examines the effectiveness of AI-assisted tasks in enhancing foreign language learning, focusing on their role in developing learners' linguistic competence, communicative skills, motivation, and autonomy. It explores various AI-supported activities, including vocabulary and grammar exercises, conversational simulations, pronunciation practice, listening and reading comprehension, writing assistance, and personalized assessments. These tasks offer learners individualized learning experiences, immediate feedback, and opportunities for interactive practice tailored to their proficiency levels and educational needs. It concludes that the pedagogically appropriate use of AI-assisted tasks has considerable potential to enhance foreign language learning outcomes and create more personalized, engaging, and accessible learning environments.

items.title: The effects of parental psychological control and career decision-making self-efficacy on college students’ employment anxiety: the mediating role of motivational regulation
items.abstract: Employment anxiety has become an important issue affecting college students’ psychological well-being and career development, yet its underlying mechanisms require further investigation. Based on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study examined associations of parental psychological control and career decision-making self-efficacy on college students’ employment anxiety, and further explored the mediating roles of identified regulation and external regulation. A questionnaire survey was conducted among 509 junior undergraduate students facing the upcoming graduation and job-search period. Participants completed the Future Employment Anxiety Scale, Parental Psychological Control Scale, Career Decision-Making Self-Efficacy Scale, and Work Extrinsic and Intrinsic Motivation Scale (WEIMS). Structural equation modeling and the Bootstrap method were employed to examine the relationships among the variables. The results showed that: (1) Parental psychological control was significantly and positively associated with college students’ employment anxiety, whereas career decision-making self-efficacy significantly and negatively associated with employment anxiety in statistical prediction; (2) Parental psychological control was significantly and negatively associated with identified regulation and external regulation, while career decision-making self-efficacy was significantly and positively associated with both types of motivational regulation; (3) Identified regulation and external regulation served as parallel statistical mediators in the associations between parental psychological control, career decision-making self-efficacy, and employment anxiety; and (4) Further analysis revealed that both types of motivational regulation showed masking patterns opposite to the directions of the direct statistical effects, suggesting that different forms of motivational regulation may be simultaneously linked to career engagement and higher anxiety in employment contexts. This study elucidates the psychological mechanisms through which family environment, individual psychological resources, and motivational regulation are jointly associated with employment anxiety, providing theoretical implications for employment-related psychological interventions in higher education.

items.title: The GenAI Who Knew Too Little: Revisiting Transactive Memory Systems in Human GenAI Collaboration
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly transforming knowledge work, creating new collaborative dynamics that challenge tradi-tional human-human interaction patterns. This study investigates how Transactive Memory Systems (TMS) manifest in human-GenAI collabora-tion. Through qualitative interpretive interviews with 14 knowledge work-ers and thematic analysis, we identified distinct TMS manifestations across its three main dimensions: (1) regarding specialization, expertise recogni-tion exhibited asymmetry. Humans developed awareness of GenAI capabili-ties while GenAI demonstrated only temporary recognition of human exper-tise; (2) in terms of credibility, humans formed ambivalent trust relation-ships with GenAI, simultaneously attributing expertise to the latter while implementing additional verification processes; and (3) concerning coor-dination, where humans primarily directed more passive GenAI systems lacking initiative, resulting in hierarchical interaction patterns and unidi-rectional information flow. Our findings reveal that TMS manifests differ-ently in human-GenAI compared to human-human collaboration, necessitat-ing theoretical adaptations including trust markers, acknowledging GenAI's absent metamemory, and identifying its temporary memory.

items.title: The hospital as a third classroom: a qualitative descriptive-interpretive study of situated learning and the hidden curriculum among medical interns
items.abstract: Abstract Background Much medical training occurs through everyday clinical work, where informal teaching and the hidden curriculum shape learning and professional identity. Social pedagogy offers a relational and ethical lens for these processes. We explored interns’ experiences of the hospital as a third classroom: a workplace learning environment alongside university teaching and the formal internship programme. Methods We conducted a qualitative descriptive-interpretive study in an urban private hospital in Ecuador. Twenty-one rotating medical interns from the 2024–2025 cohort completed an anonymous online questionnaire with 10 open-ended questions in July 2025. Responses were examined through complete reading, open inductive coding, identification of meaning units, thematic grouping and a double-entry matrix. Social pedagogy informed interpretation. Reported institutional expectations provided documentary context, rather than a separately reported documentary analysis. Results Three related themes were identified. The hospital functioned as a situated learning community through bedside participation, corridor microteaching, night-shift learning, role modelling and patient and family education. The hidden curriculum and ethical climate influenced whether interns could ask questions, acknowledge uncertainty and develop respectful professional identities. Accessible tutors, interprofessional rounds and humanising practices bridged formal intentions and everyday learning, whereas workload, rigid hierarchy, inconsistent feedback and service-level variation restricted educational opportunities. Together, the themes describe learning opportunities, the relationships governing participation and the organisational conditions supporting or constraining them. Conclusions In this cohort, social pedagogy helped interpret the relational, participatory and ethical dimensions of workplace learning. Protecting brief teaching moments, responding respectfully to uncertainty and reflecting interprofessionally on hidden messages are potential implications for clinical teachers; their feasibility and effects require evaluation.

items.title: The Impact of AI-Generated Content on Trust and Authenticity in Social Media Communication: A Study of Three Australian Case Studies
items.abstract: The robust growth of generative artificial intelligence (AI), especially large language models and image-generation systems, has greatly shaped communication practices on social media. In this context, AI-generated content has become widely adopted by businesses, media organizations, influencers, and individual users to efficiently create text, images, videos, and interactive content. While these technologies boost creativity and communication productivity, they also introduce ethical concerns regarding transparency, authenticity, misinformation, and public trust. This study investigates how AI-generated content influences trust and authenticity in social media communication through a qualitative interpretive case study approach. Three representative cases, the Georgie Purcell AI image controversy, the AI-generated "Aboriginal Steve Irwin" incident, and the Jeanswest AI-generated advertising backlash, are investigated using secondary sources including academic literature, news reports, organizational statements, and public responses. Based on this analytical framework, AI ethics principles of transparency, accountability, fairness, and human oversight are applied to guide the analysis. The findings suggest that generative AI has reshaped social media communication by improving efficiency and personalization while disrupting authenticity assessment. Therefore, public trust relies on transparent AI disclosure, ethical governance, and responsible practices. Moreover, sustainable AI integration requires stronger governance, platform transparency, and human oversight to maintain communication credibility.

items.title: The Impact Of Artificial Intelligence Usage On Learning Effectiveness and Academic Motivation Among University Students
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly influenced higher education, including the emergence of AI-based learning applications such as ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Perplexity. While prior studies have examined the role of AI in general academic settings, limited attention has been given to its use within vocational, practice-based education, where learning outcomes are closely tied to technical skill development. This study aims to describe vocational students' perceptions of AI use in learning, particularly in relation to learning effectiveness and academic motivation, among students at a vocational institution in Palembang. A quantitative descriptive design using the survey method was employed, involving 50 respondents selected through purposive sampling based on their active use of AI-based learning applications. Data were collected through a 15-item Likert-scale questionnaire distributed online and analyzed descriptively using frequency and percentage distributions. The findings indicate that most respondents held positive perceptions of AI, particularly regarding its role in helping them understand lecture material, complete assignments more efficiently, and study independently. However, perceptions were more divided regarding the accuracy of AI-generated information and its contribution to time management, suggesting that the perceived benefits of AI are not uniform across all aspects of learning. Respondents also emphasized that AI cannot replace the role of lecturers. These findings suggest that, when used appropriately alongside critical thinking and lecturer guidance, AI is perceived by vocational students as a supportive tool for practice-based learning. items.title: The Influence Of Leadership, Work Culture, And Intrinsic Motivation On Teacher Performance Through Job Satisfaction At SMAN 1 Kuala Langkat Regency
items.abstract: This study aims to test and analyze the influence of leadership, work culture, and intrinsic motivation on teacher performance through job satisfaction at SMA Negeri 1 Kuala, Lalat Regency. This study uses a quantitative approach with a survey method. The population in this study is all teachers at SMA Negeri 1 Kuala as many as 60 people. Because the population is less than 100 people, the entire population is used as a research sample. Data was collected through a questionnaire with a Likert scale and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling through the SmartPLS 3.0 program. The results of the study show that leadership has a positive and significant effect on teacher performance and job satisfaction. Work culture also has a positive and significant effect on teacher performance and job satisfaction. Intrinsic motivation has a positive and significant effect on teacher performance and job satisfaction. In addition, job satisfaction has a positive and significant effect on teacher performance. The results of the indirect influence test showed that job satisfaction was able to mediate the influence of leadership, work culture, and intrinsic motivation on teacher performance. The R-square value shows that leadership, work culture, and intrinsic motivation can explain job satisfaction by 40.4%. Meanwhile, leadership, work culture, intrinsic motivation, and job satisfaction were able to explain teacher performance by 51%. Thus, improving teacher performance can be done through strengthening the principal's leadership, a positive work culture, intrinsic motivation of teachers, and job satisfaction.

items.title: The Judge Under Trial: Monte Carlo Verification of the Reasoning-Aligned Rubric Tuning Lifecycle
items.abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) as automated evaluators—commonly termed LLM-as-a-Judge—introduces a critical vulnerability: the “right answer, wrong reason” failure mode, where a judge reaches the correct verdict through unsound reasoning that is invisible to standard label-agreement dashboards. Kong et al. [1] propose Reasoning-Aligned Rubric Tuning (RART) to address this, anchoring the judge’s rationale to human judgment via a Meta-Judge and iterative rubric refinement. This paper presents a reproducible Monte Carlo simulation (300 replicates, 40 iterations) that empirically verifies the RART lifecycle against a label-only baseline (Vanilla). We formally model the latent rubric state θ_R = (q_R, b_R), the noisy meta-judge detection layer, the biased reflector update, and the statistical drift monitor. Our results confirm the framework’s central thesis. While Vanilla achieves marginally higher final label accuracy (q_R = 0.956) than RART (q_R = 0.875), its reasoning alignment collapses entirely (b_R = −0.842), whereas RART stabilizes reasoning (b_R = +0.910). Furthermore, the simulation visually exposes the structural vulnerabilities of the framework: Vanilla consumes 2.6× the computational budget (39.4 vs 14.8 iterations) due to the stopping-rule artifact; the standard 2σ drift band produces an unacceptable 11.3% false-alarm rate at K = 3 raters; and the blind-spot leak between shared judge-generator architectures decays only when human oversight (p_H > 0) is present. The simulation serves as both a pedagogical tool and an empirical validation that the LLM judge is an amplifier of human judgment, not a replacement for it.

items.title: The Labor of Storytelling: How People with Chronic Illnesses Leverage AI and Communities for Narrative Translation
items.abstract: The distinctiveness of people with chronic illness as storytellers is how they experience their illness. Symptoms, pain, and biological disruptions are eloquent forms of speech of the body that beget social articulation. The stories people tell about illness shape how suffering is legitimized, and acted upon. Large language models have emerged as new mediators within this landscape---a role once predominantly supported by communities. In doing so, these systems participate in what we term narrative translation: transforming lived illness experiences for particular audiences and purposes. Through 21 prototype-driven semi-structured interviews with people with chronic illness, we contribute an empirical account of how participants navigate this mediation alongside existing sources of support. Our findings surface distinct yet complementary roles participants envisioned for AI and their communities, and how trust in AI was shaped by learning model-boundaries and perceiving understanding. We characterize these findings to inform future designs of AI-mediated narrative support.

items.abstract: The service quality of public sector organisations in Botswana is generally considered to be less satisfactory than the private sector. One of the myriads of reasons is arguably reward and punishment system not being applied firmly and consistently. This research investigates the relationship between reward system and employee attraction and retention, as well as the extent to which these rewards influence workforce stability in the public health sector in Botswana. The study adopted a pragmatist approach using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. Employing semi-structured face-tox-face interviews and structured questionnaire to a stratified random sample of 228 doctors and nurses for data collection. For qualitative Thematic coding and categorisation for qualitative, while SPSS version 20.0, employing descriptive statistics and linear regression analysis were used. The linear regression analysis revealed that extrinsic rewards significantly drive employee attraction, while intrinsic rewards are the strongest predictors of retention. Social rewards play a complementary yet significant role, reinforcing the need for a balanced and integrated total reward system. To ensure loyalty, commitment and retain self-motivated star performers within the public health institutions in Botswana, it is critical that managers engender and place high premium on employees’ intrinsic rewards among others. The empirical evidence clearly demonstrates the positive effect organisational support, both in cash and in kind, have on the employees of the public health sector, confirming that enhanced intrinsic motivation and rewards is a predictor of employee attraction and retention.

items.title: The Political Economy of Artificial Intelligence: Energy, Human Dignity, and Social Contract Theory
items.abstract: This article investigates the political economy of artificial intelligence by examining the relationships among technological development, energy availability, and financial dynamics. Drawing on social contract theory, it considers how these transformations may affect human dignity, social cooperation, and the institutional distribution of opportunities, resources, and responsibilities, while distinguishing observable consequences from hypotheses that require empirical verification. The analysis argues that energy constraints, computing capacity, financial expectations, and the displacement of professional and managerial work should be assessed within an integrated framework that neither attributes autonomous agency to AI systems nor regards their social effects as technologically predetermined. On this basis, the article proposes a governance framework that combines technical oversight, labor protection, redistributive measures, and international cooperation. The adequacy of this framework should be evaluated in terms of measurable effects on employment, wages, productivity, public finances, and the distribution of the benefits of innovation. At a time when the accelerated deployment of artificial intelligence is concentrating technological and financial power, increasing pressure on energy systems, and exposing labor markets and democratic institutions to disruptive change, the article argues that the central issue is no longer whether AI will transform society, but who will govern that transformation, bear its costs, and appropriate its benefits; without effective public oversight and distributive safeguards, technological progress risks deepening inequality, weakening social cohesion, and undermining the material foundations of human dignity.

items.title: The Prosocial Turn in Video Games: A Twenty-Year Shift in the Motivations Games Simulate
items.abstract: As video games have grown from a niche pastime into a major cultural medium, they have reached broader audiences and transformed the social context of play, whether alone or with others. We ask whether the motivations engaged by the games themselves have changed over time. In Study 1, we used a large language model, validated against human coding, to annotate 11,359 commercially released games from 1993 to 2016 on 48 motivational ingredients, including status-seeking, revenge, affiliation, compassion, and curiosity. We normalized within each game to represent its relative motivational composition. Over this period, the average competitive index (the share of a game’s motivational content devoted to competition, dominance, and aggression) fell from 41% to 26%, while the prosocial index (affiliation, warmth, and care) rose from 11% to 24%. This reallocation held within genres and franchises, in both single- and multiplayer titles, and under all 642,560 admissible definitions of the two indices. In Study 2, 4,498 players reported their favorite games and completed a Big Five measure. Higher Agreeableness predicted a balance favoring prosocial over agonistic content, driven primarily by lower agonistic content, whereas higher Extraversion, particularly Sociability, predicted a balance favoring agonistic content. This contrast suggests that a disposition towards social engagement is distinct from a preference for caring social content. Together, the studies document a “prosocial turn” in the motivational content of video games: a historical reallocation from competition and dominance towards affiliation, warmth, and care. The direction of this shift aligns with contemporary personality differences in content preference.

items.title: The rise of super-emotional intelligence
items.abstract: The debate about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) runs along a single axis: cognitive capability and its projected culmination in superintelligence. We argue that this framing leaves a complementary axis unexamined and propose the goal of Super-Emotional Intelligence (SEI): systems that perceive, model, regulate, and respond to affect better than skilled human experts, while remaining human-centered. SEI is a performance construct realized by a functional architecture, not a claim about machine experience, and we give measurable criteria for each of its four capacities. Today's affect-aware AI, from multimodal emotion recognition to empathic chatbots, recognizes, or simulates emotion at or below human level and is judged against human ceilings. Three things would set SEI apart: perception that adds peripheral and contactless physiological channels, none of them emotion-specific, but some, like the vestigial ear muscles, resolving affective processing at the timescale of the events that evoke it; a generative model of affect grounded in active inference rather than pattern matching; and functional allostatic self-regulation. The decisive gap in current systems is architectural. A sensed state conditions a prompt, but nothing carries a state estimate across turns, models the effect of the system's own responses, or selects actions under an explicit objective. We specify such a closed loop, state the conditions under which it is stable and steerable rather than manipulative, propose a preregistered validation plan whose failure would falsify our claims, and treat governance as a design constraint of the loop rather than an afterthought.

items.title: The Role of Edge Computing in Future 6G Wireless Networks: A Literature Review
items.abstract: The rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI), autonomous systems, and immersive applications is creating new demands on wireless networks. Although 5G has improved data rates, latency, and device connectivity, applications such as autonomous driving, AI-enabled robotics, virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and smart healthcare require fast and intelligent processing as well as communication. Traditional cloud computing depends on centralised data centres, which can increase latency and core-network traffic when large amounts of data are produced at the edge. Edge computing addresses this limitation by moving computing resources closer to users and data sources. This paper reviews the role of edge computing in future sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks. It introduces the 6G vision and edge computing, compares edge and cloud computing, examines major benefits and applications, and discusses key challenges including security, resource management, energy efficiency, scalability, and service continuity. The paper argues that a device-edge-cloud architecture will be important for future intelligent wireless networks.

items.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence to Predict Visual Outcome in Patients With Macular Pucker
items.abstract: Purpose: To assess the current role of artificial intelligence (AI) to predict postoperative best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) after macular pucker surgery using optical coherence tomography (OCT) data. Methods: A systematic search was conducted of PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library. Data extraction included study design, demographics, AI model characteristics, and performance metrics. Study quality was assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment + Artificial Intelligence tool, and results were synthesized narratively. Results: Six studies involving 2728 patients (65–71 years) were analyzed. Convolutional neural networks and gradient boosting decision trees were applied to predict postoperative BCVA. The convolutional neural networks ResNet-101 and Inception-ResNet-V2 outperformed human grading, with ResNet-101 achieving the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.97). Interpretability techniques identified ectopic inner foveal layers (EIFL) and irregular inner nuclear layer-outer plexiform layer as key predictors. Conclusions: Deep learning models demonstrate potential in predicting postoperative outcomes from preoperative OCT scans after macular pucker surgery. Advanced architectures such as ResNet-101 and Inception-ResNet-v2 outperform simpler models and expert grading. However, clinical translation depends on model generalizability, interpretability, real-time application, and inclusion of functional data. Future research should emphasize multicenter validation to ensure broader applicability.

items.title: The Value-Normative System of the Culture of Artificial Intelligence: An Anthropological Turn in the Age of “Smart” Networks
items.abstract: The article describes the principal sociocultural states produced within the culture of artificial intelligence (CAI): civilizational, substantial, axiological vacuum, inversion, and destructive. It is noted that all of these states can be observed almost simultaneously, owing to the rapid pace at which the AI culture is developing. The article assesses how these states relate to the anthropological turn, which entails a reconsideration of the human role in cultural practices: AI acts as a tool that expands human capabilities rather than replacing them. In the “human + machine” framework, fundamental cultural categories – primarily authorship and creativity – are being trans-formed. Authorship becomes distributed and is increasingly interpreted as a property of the “human + algo-rithm” system, whereas creativity remains the prerogative of humans with their capacity to formulate tasks, in-terpret results, endow them with meaning and assume responsibility for what is created. At the same time, hu-mans retain a leading role: rather than adapting to the logic of the machine, they direct and make sense of its operation. The study of CAI and its value-normative system is necessary because it helps us understand the large-scale shifts in cultural practices and value orientations caused by the spread of these technologies.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Toward AI-Augmented Applied Systems: Emerging AI and LLM Directions Across Trajectory Prediction, Cybersecurity, and Engineering Automation
items.abstract: This paper reviews fifteen recent publications (2015-2026) spanning trajectory prediction, cybersecurity and trust management, classical machine learning and algorithmic optimisation, and engineering automation, and asks a forward-looking question: where is artificial intelligence — particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), foundation models, and agentic AI systems — positioned to extend each of these research directions next? For each of four thematic clusters we first summarise the current method documented in the reviewed sources, then discuss a concrete, currently-emerging AI direction grounded in recent (2025-2026) literature: LLM- and foundation-model-based trajectory reasoning for Cluster A; agentic, LLM-driven security-operations copilots for Cluster B, including a reported 6.5x improvement in malicious-alert identification over human analysts in one production deployment; learned and graph-neural-network-based approaches to the classical optimisation and graph-isomorphism problems in Cluster C; and natural-language-to-workflow agentic automation for the low-code and embedded-systems work in Cluster D. Throughout, we explicitly separate what the reviewed papers themselves established from this review's own forward-looking analysis, and close with a discussion of the reliability, interpretability, and adversarial-robustness risks that accompany each proposed direction.
